description: Expose bounded low-cardinality runtime signals, tri-state OTel health, anomalous route amplification, and per-request agent-path work counts without making observability part of business state or feeding the built-in collector back into itself.

tasks.title: Deliver actionable tri-state OTel runtime status
tasks.description: Replace the history-counting collector status with a process-local RuntimeObservability state, deterministic process/storage sampling, ingestion outcome counters, independent degradation sources, and a fixed status API payload rendered by mo otel status. Wire normal collector startup into the same state, preserve core health, and establish the complete Mohist.Server.Runtime Meter catalog without exporting it to the built-in receiver; the routes array is present and bounded but remains empty until T-003 supplies request diagnostics.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /otel/api/status remains available while the Server is reachable and returns exactly off, healthy, or degraded: off when Mohist:Otel:Enabled is false; enabled startup remains degraded/unverified until collector bind and the first bounded storage probe succeed; healthy requires usable collection/storage and no active protection source.

The fixed ApiResponse data shape contains status, collector_online, process start time, storage usage/budget/growth window, received/saved/rejected/dropped Span-attempt counters, CPU utilization, working-set bytes, GC heap bytes, nullable latest degradation, and a bounded routes array; unavailable samples are null rather than fabricated zero values.

TraceQuerier.GetStatusAsync and CollectorStatusSnapshot are removed, status generation performs no Trace/Span COUNT(*) or history enumeration, and tests with small versus large unrelated Trace history observe the same bounded operations and response shape.

RuntimeObservability creates the exact Mohist.Server.Runtime instruments, kinds, units, and attribute-key contracts listed in design D2; a MeterListener contract test locks the full catalog and proves project, issue, workflow, session, Trace, Span, and raw-URL identities cannot appear as labels.

No MeterProvider/OTLP metric exporter sends Mohist.Server.Runtime metrics to the built-in receiver; existing OTel ingestion, query, status, exporter, and direct otel.db work remain excluded from recursive Trace/metric feedback, with automated tests proving processing terminates without equivalent self-generated signals.

The current ingester reports one typed IngestOutcome per parsed request attempt: duplicate upserts count as saved, pre-parse admission failures do not count as received, malformed parsed Spans count as dropped, retryable transaction rollback activates storage_write without counting dropped, and rejected is reserved for later non-retryable partial-success protection paths.

The enabled-only sampler runs immediately and then every 10 seconds through injected TimeProvider, computes normalized CPU from process-time deltas, combines otel.db/WAL/SHM size against the fixed 1-GiB budget, computes growth from a fixed 60-second seven-slot ring, emits null until two valid samples exist, and allows only one bounded probe in flight while coalescing ticks and cancelling cleanly on shutdown; a successful sample followed by a failed sample invalidates cached values and causes observable gauges/status to report unavailable rather than stale data.

Degradation is tracked by independent collector, storage_read, storage_write, and ingest_protection sources; rejection/drop protection expires after five injected minutes, storage sources clear only on their corresponding success, and latest bounded degradation code/message/time remains available after recovery. Structured transition logs contain PreviousState, NewState, ReasonCode, and Reason and occur exactly once for healthy-to-degraded and degraded-to-healthy transitions without repeats during a stable state.

mo otel status validates the new status field, exits successfully for off/healthy/degraded, renders State, Collector, Storage, Telemetry, Process, Latest degradation, and the empty Routes section, and fails clearly against the old status payload; server-unreachable behavior remains unchanged.

When observability is off, the OTLP listener, trace exporter, sampler and storage-maintenance work do not run; RuntimeObservability remains only to serve the off snapshot, and no recording or background collection occurs.
An unreadable OTel database or failed write yields degraded with an actionable reason while GET /api/health continues returning its normal successful status=ok response.

Unit/spec coverage uses FakeTimeProvider, fake process/storage readers, in-memory SQLite and operation counters only; no host filesystem, real network, wall-clock wait, elapsed-time assertion, or external metrics backend is used. npm test passes, including server and CLI tests with warnings treated as errors.
tasks.output: A usable /otel/api/status and mo otel status tri-state surface backed by new bounded runtime observability, sampler, ingestion/degradation state and metric-contract modules under packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Otel and Infrastructure/Hosting, normal startup/OTLP wiring and CLI rendering, plus focused server and CLI tests.
tasks.notes: This is the first user-visible vertical slice: operators can diagnose normal collector/storage/process/ingestion state even before route amplification is added; T-002 hardens the separate bind-failure recovery path. Keep Mohist:Otel:Enabled default false for #472. Register RuntimeObservability even when off, but do not run recording or sampling. Preserve the snake-case status wire contract in design D7 and the no-compatibility deployment rule (new CLI before Server). This task also establishes the publication seams consumed by #437/#471 and the idle request/path instruments completed by T-003/T-004; do not implement those follow-up policies here. Relevant additional requirements: specs/runtime-observability-metrics/spec.md#runtime-signals-are-available-through-a-standard-meter-and-a-local-summary, specs/runtime-observability-metrics/spec.md#metric-identity-has-stable-low-cardinality, specs/runtime-observability-metrics/spec.md#built-in-observability-work-cannot-observe-itself-into-a-feedback-loop, and the otel-runtime-status requirements except the bind-fallback scenario owned by T-002 and route-summary scenarios owned by T-003.

tasks.title: Preserve degraded status through OTLP bind fallback
tasks.description: Harden the OTLP-port bind-failure path so the failed host and all partially started services are disposed before one alternate main-API host starts, while preserving the user's enabled observability intent in RuntimeObservability. Report collector_bind_failed as degraded instead of rewriting configuration to off, and prove core API readiness and single-instance hosted work survive the fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic injected host-start/bind-failure seam exercises the fallback without a real network socket or process; the failed WebApplication and its partially started hosted services are stopped and disposed before alternate-host construction begins.

The alternate host omits the OTLP Kestrel listener but does not rewrite Mohist:Otel:Enabled=false; RuntimeObservability retains configured enabled intent and exposes degraded, collector_online=false, and latest reason code collector_bind_failed through /otel/api/status and mo otel status.

Fallback verification proves exactly one Orleans silo, one diagnostics sampler, and one main API host remain active, with no duplicate timers, transition logs, exporters, or background maintenance from the failed host.

GET /api/health and the main API remain successful after fallback, while the OTLP path is unreachable because no collector listener exists; observability failure does not change business results or Workflow/Runner behavior.

A normal successful start still clears collector_unverified exactly once and reports collector_online=true; the fallback changes no off-state behavior and emits no repeated degraded transition log while the bind failure remains active.
Focused startup/bind-fallback unit and integration specs use fakes or in-process hosts only, and npm test passes with warnings treated as errors.
tasks.output: Refactored packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Program.cs host-start/fallback lifecycle integrated with RuntimeObservability, deterministic host lifecycle test seams, and startup/fallback specs proving one surviving host/silo/sampler and accurate degraded status.
tasks.notes: This is a complete failure-path slice: after it lands, a collector port conflict remains diagnosable while core Mohist keeps running. Do not use a real occupied port in tests; inject the start/failure and disposal boundaries. The alternate host suppresses only the OTLP listener, not configured observability intent.

tasks.title: Expose bounded HTTP route amplification diagnostics
tasks.description: Add one ambient request-work scope and infrastructure adapters that count business EF commands, caller-side Orleans invocations, and physical HttpClientFactory sends, then publish stable-route request metrics and a bounded five-minute route summary through the status API and CLI created by T-001. Keep all OTel endpoints and storage work outside the scope, and make route identity, method/status normalization, bucket limits, ordering, restart behavior, and fake-time expiry deterministic.
acceptanceCriteria: RuntimeRequestMetricsMiddleware runs after routing and before endpoint execution when OTel is enabled, completes exactly once in finally, uses RouteEndpoint.RoutePattern.RawText or the bounded unmatched fallback, normalizes methods to GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD/OPTIONS/OTHER and invalid status codes to 0, and never labels a concrete URL or resource identity.

The request scope counts each business MohistDbContext command, each caller-side Orleans invocation begun in the active HTTP execution context, and each physical factory-created HTTP send including retries; atomic increments remain correct under awaited parallel fan-out, and all adapters no-op outside an active scope without changing call results.

OTel ingestion, query, status and maintenance create no request-work scope; direct otel.db operations are not counted as business database calls, and self-feedback tests prove these paths emit no equivalent route/database/downstream signal back to the built-in collector.

Request completion records the existing request-count, duration, database-call and downstream-call instruments with only the locked low-cardinality HTTP attributes; MeterListener tests assert exact labels and values for distinct concrete project/issue/session URLs sharing one route template.

The local route aggregator uses 301 one-second buckets, at most 256 stable routes plus other per bucket, and at most 301*257 retained aggregates; it allows less than one second of boundary over-retention, expires observations after that tolerance through FakeTimeProvider, and starts empty after Server restart without business persistence.

Snapshot aggregation exposes at most 10 entries with route, request_count, average_duration_ms, max_duration_ms, database_calls_per_request, and downstream_calls_per_request, ordered by total calls-per-request descending then average latency descending; zero-request division cannot produce NaN or infinity.

GET /otel/api/status returns the bounded recent routes from RuntimeObservability without database/filesystem/downstream work, and mo otel status renders the same ordered route rows while all storage, ingestion, process, degradation, and three-state behavior from T-001 remains unchanged.

Tests cover more than 10 routes, more than 256 route identities, unmatched paths, normalized custom methods/statuses, parallel calls, retry counting, one-second/five-minute boundaries, deterministic tie ordering, restart-local state, and the absence of an external metric reader; they use operation counts and fake time, not wall-clock duration. A route-registration guard enumerates application route templates and fails if legitimate registered routes exceed the 256-route budget and would fold into other.
npm test passes, including the runtime observability unit tests and status API/CLI specs with warnings treated as errors.
tasks.output: Request-work middleware and EF/Orleans/HttpClient accounting adapters, bounded route aggregation and metric recording under packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Otel and Infrastructure/Hosting, populated status API/CLI Routes output, and focused route-metric/self-feedback tests.
tasks.notes: Count physical work at the boundaries defined by design D3; do not infer costs from Activities and do not attempt transitive attribution after an Orleans message boundary. The route section was introduced as an empty fixed-shape field by T-001, so this task fills it without another wire-contract migration. Do not persist route buckets or add an OTLP metrics exporter. T-002 and this task are independent after T-001 and may run in parallel. This task provides RequestWorkScope and RecordAgentPath semantics consumed by T-004.

tasks.title: Expose agent status and activity amplification
tasks.description: Add one fixed amplification object to the existing project-scoped agent status and activity responses, populated from explicit candidate/processed/transcript observations and the request-local database/downstream counters delivered by T-003. Emit the three agent-path Meter observations with bounded path identities while preserving all existing response fields, ordering, limits, route scope, and business behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentStatusResponse and ActivityDto each include amplification with non-negative camelCase fields candidates, processed, transcriptRecords, databaseCalls, and downstreamCalls; the object is present for empty results and zero processed values never produce a missing, infinite, or computed-ratio sentinel.

For GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/agent/status, candidates equals Session records inspected for active-agent classification, processed equals active-agent records returned, transcriptRecords is zero for the current path, and databaseCalls/downstreamCalls cover the same completed HTTP request including runner and workflow lookups.

For GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/agent/activity, candidates equals the bounded Session set loaded before reconciliation, processed equals cards returned after reconciliation, transcriptRecords counts every transcript record actually materialized by latest-event and reduction reads, and databaseCalls/downstreamCalls share that same request boundary.

The existing status fields, activity summary/cards/waiting items, ordering, limit clamping and maximum 200 cards remain unchanged; the removed unscoped /api/agent/status and /api/agent/activity routes remain absent and only project-scoped routes gain the object.

RuntimeObservability records path candidates, processed and transcript-record histograms using only mohist.path=agent.status or agent.activity; no project, issue, workflow, session or raw-URL identity enters labels.
Amplification observations remain runtime-only: no MohistDbContext schema, Orleans state, Workflow, AgentSession, issue or scheduling decision is written or changed because of a counter value.

Tests cover status candidates filtered to fewer active agents, empty status, activity reconciliation, transcript materialization, response-limit overflow, and short versus history-heavy datasets; they assert the actual operation counts and fixed response shape without requiring #467 status optimization or #468 persisted activity summaries.
Focused agent route/assembler specs and MeterListener tests pass, and npm test completes with warnings treated as errors and no wall-clock assertions.
tasks.output: Updated project-scoped agent status/activity DTOs and routes, explicit observations in WorkflowActivityQuerier and AgentActivityFeedAssembler/transcript reads, bounded agent-path metrics, and focused server tests under packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.SpecTests/Specs/AgentOps and Sessions.
tasks.notes: This task exposes current amplification; it must not absorb the optimizations owned by dependent issues #467 and #468. Count transcript records each time they are materialized, even when two reductions read the same stored part, because the metric describes work rather than unique facts. Database/downstream counts come from T-003's RequestWorkScope; candidate/processed/transcript counts stay next to the operations defining them. Relevant additional requirements: specs/agent-path-amplification/spec.md#agent-activity-exposes-transcript-and-fan-out-work, #agent-amplification-reporting-remains-bounded, and #amplification-signals-are-operational-data-only.
